name: A1.1.1 System Resource Monitoring Implementation
description:
The organization shall implement and maintain monitoring capabilities for critical system resources across all infrastructure components. This includes establishing automated monitoring for CPU utilization, memory consumption, storage capacity, and network bandwidth. Monitoring tools shall be configured to collect metrics at appropriate intervals and retain historical data sufficient for trend analysis. Alert thresholds shall be defined and documented to notify appropriate personnel when resource utilization approaches critical levels.

Implementation: CloudWatch collects Lambda invocation, duration, and memory metrics. Alert thresholds defined.

name: A1.1.2 Capacity Planning and Forecasting
description:
The organization shall establish a capacity planning process that includes regular review of resource utilization trends and forecasting of future capacity requirements. This process shall consider business growth projections, seasonal variations, and planned system changes. Capacity assessments shall be conducted at least annually, with documented plans for capacity expansion when utilization trends indicate potential resource constraints. The organization shall maintain documented procedures for scaling infrastructure resources to meet anticipated demand.

Implementation: Historical metrics retained for trend analysis. DocumentDB storage growth tracked. Annual capacity review in board meetings.

name: A1.1 The entity maintains, monitors, and evaluates current processing capacity and use of system components (infras
description:
A1.1 (A1 - Availability Criteria): The entity maintains, monitors, and evaluates current processing capacity and use of system components (infrastructure, data, and software) to manage capacity demand and to enable the implementation of additional capacity to help meet its objectives.

Monitor your system resources to ensure you have enough capacity to meet demand. Track CPU, memory, storage, and network usage, forecast future needs based on growth trends, and add capacity before you run out. This prevents slowdowns or outages due to resource exhaustion.

Implementation: CloudWatch monitors Lambda and DocumentDB capacity. Alarms trigger on threshold breaches.

name: A1.2.1 Cloud Infrastructure Environmental Protection and Redundancy
description:
The organization shall ensure that cloud service providers maintain appropriate environmental protections and redundancy capabilities for hosted infrastructure. This includes verification that cloud providers implement physical security controls, redundant power systems, fire suppression, climate control, and geographic redundancy. For a remote-first technology company of this size, reliance on enterprise cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) satisfies environmental protection requirements, provided proper due diligence is documented.

Implementation: AWS provides physical security, redundant power, environmental controls per SOC 2.

name: A1.2.2 Data Backup and Recovery Procedures
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain comprehensive data backup procedures to ensure business continuity and data protection. This includes automated backup configurations for all critical systems and data, offsite or geographically distributed backup storage, defined retention periods aligned with business requirements, and documented recovery procedures. Backup integrity shall be verified through regular restoration testing to confirm recoverability.

Implementation: DocumentDB: automated daily backups, 7-day retention, PITR enabled.

name: A1.2.3 Disaster Recovery Planning and Testing
description:
The organization shall maintain a disaster recovery plan that addresses alternate processing capabilities and recovery procedures in the event of primary system failure. The plan shall define recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO) for critical systems, document failover procedures, and identify responsible personnel. The disaster recovery plan shall be tested at least annually to validate effectiveness and updated based on test results and organizational changes.

Implementation: Multi-AZ deployment across 3 availability zones. Humadroid BCP dashboard shows RTO: AWS Infrastructure 2hrs. Q1 2025 DR test completed with 100% success rate.

name: A1.2 The entity authorizes, designs, develops or acquires, implements, operates, approves, and maintains environmen
description:
A1.2 (A1 - Availability Criteria): The entity authorizes, designs, develops or acquires, implements, operates, approves, and maintains environmental protections, backup processes, and recovery infrastructure to meet its objectives.

Protect your systems from environmental threats and ensure you can recover from disasters. This includes physical protections (like fire suppression and backup power), regular data backups stored offsite, and alternate processing capabilities if your primary site fails. Test your backup and recovery procedures regularly.

Implementation: AWS SOC 2 certified data centers. DocumentDB: daily backups, 7-day retention, PITR enabled, multi-AZ.

name: A1.3.1 Recovery Plan Testing Schedule and Execution
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal schedule for testing recovery plan procedures at least annually. Given the remote work environment and small team size, testing shall include scenarios relevant to distributed operations such as cloud service failover, remote access restoration, and data recovery from backup systems. Tests shall be documented with clear objectives, scope, and success criteria defined prior to execution. All key personnel shall participate in testing exercises appropriate to their roles.

Implementation: Q1 2025 BCP Full Test executed Feb 4, 2026. Plan: AWS Service Disruption Recovery. Coordinator: Mo Messidi. Scenario: Full Systems recovery from backups using IaC.

name: A1.3.2 Recovery Test Results Documentation and Plan Updates
description:
The organization shall formally document the results of all recovery plan tests, including any deficiencies, failures, or areas for improvement identified during testing. Test results shall be reviewed by appropriate personnel, and the recovery plan shall be updated to address identified gaps or lessons learned. A tracking mechanism shall be maintained to ensure all identified issues are remediated and incorporated into updated recovery procedures within a reasonable timeframe.

Implementation: Q1 2025 test results: Status Completed, Success Rate 100%, Result: System recovered successfully. Plan Status: Active. Total Exercises: 1.

name: A1.3 The entity tests recovery plan procedures supporting system recovery to meet its objectives.
description:
A1.3 (A1 - Availability Criteria): The entity tests recovery plan procedures supporting system recovery to meet its objectives.

Regularly test your ability to recover from various disaster scenarios. Include tests of data restoration, failover to backup systems, and operation from alternate locations. Involve key personnel in tests, document results, and update plans based on what you learn. Testing reveals problems before you face a real disaster.

Implementation: Q1 2025 BCP test completed Feb 4, 2026: Full Systems recovery from backups using IaC. Status: Completed. Success Rate: 100%. Result: System recovered successfully.

name: C1.1.1 Confidential Information Classification Policy
description:
Establish and maintain a formal policy that defines what constitutes confidential information within the organization. The policy shall include a classification scheme (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential) with clear criteria for each level. Given the remote work environment and small team size, the policy should specifically address classification of digital assets, cloud-stored documents, and information shared via collaboration tools. The policy must identify categories of confidential information including but not limited to: trade secrets, financial data, strategic plans, customer information, pricing data, intellectual property, and partner-designated confidential materials. All team members must acknowledge understanding of the classification policy.

Implementation: 4-level classification scheme established with clear criteria per level.

name: C1.1.2 Confidential Information Identification and Labeling Procedures
description:
Implement procedures for identifying and properly labeling confidential information when created internally or received from external parties. For a remote technology company, this includes establishing naming conventions and metadata tagging for digital files, configuring document management systems to support classification labels, and defining procedures for marking confidential information in emails and shared documents. Procedures shall address how team members identify confidential information during creation, receipt, and processing activities. Regular reviews shall be conducted to ensure classification remains appropriate as information ages or business circumstances change.

Implementation: Digital file labeling and metadata tagging procedures defined.

name: C1.1.3 Confidential Information Retention and Protection Requirements
description:
Define and implement retention requirements and protection controls for confidential information based on business needs, contractual obligations, and legal requirements. For the remote work environment, establish technical controls including encryption for data at rest and in transit, access restrictions based on classification level, and secure cloud storage configurations. Implement digital equivalents of clean desk policies for remote workstations. Define retention periods for each classification level and establish legal hold procedures to prevent premature destruction of information needed for litigation or investigations. Given the small team size, assign clear ownership for confidential information management responsibilities.

Implementation: KMS encryption applied by classification. Device encryption via FileVault.

name: C1.1 The entity identifies and maintains confidential information to meet the entity's objectives related to confid
description:
C1.1 (C1 - Confidentiality Criteria): The entity identifies and maintains confidential information to meet the entity's objectives related to confidentiality.

Establish a comprehensive program for managing confidential information throughout its lifecycle. Start by defining what constitutes confidential information in your organization - this typically includes trade secrets, financial data, strategic plans, customer lists, pricing information, intellectual property, and any information marked as confidential by partners. Create procedures to identify and properly label confidential information when it's created internally or received from external parties. Implement classification schemes (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential) with clear criteria for each level. Define retention requirements for each type of confidential information based on business needs, contractual obligations, and legal requirements. Ensure confidential information is protected from unauthorized access throughout its retention period using appropriate technical controls (encryption, access restrictions) and physical controls (locked storage, clean desk policies). Prevent premature destruction by implementing hold procedures for information needed for litigation or investigations. Regular reviews ensure classification remains appropriate as information ages or circumstances change. Train employees on recognizing and properly handling confidential information.

Implementation: Data classified into 4 levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. KMS encryption by level.

name: C1.2.1 Confidential Information Disposal Policy and Procedures
description:
Establish and maintain a formal policy governing the secure disposal of confidential information. The policy shall define clear triggers for disposal including end of retention periods, project completion, contract termination, and explicit disposal requests. Document appropriate destruction methods based on data sensitivity levels: simple deletion for low-risk data, secure overwriting for moderate risk, and physical destruction or cryptographic erasure for high-risk data. For physical documents, specify cross-cut shredding requirements. Given the remote work environment, include specific guidance for disposal of confidential information on personal devices and home office equipment.

Implementation: Disposal triggers defined in policy: retention expiry, contract termination, deletion requests. KMS key deletion enables cryptographic erasure.

name: C1.2.2 Disposal Execution and Verification Records
description:
Implement a systematic process for executing and documenting the destruction of confidential information across all storage locations. Maintain detailed destruction records including what was destroyed, destruction date, method employed, responsible party, and authorizing authority. For third-party destruction services, obtain and retain certificates of destruction. Verify destruction completeness by confirming removal from all storage locations including primary systems, backups, archives, and remote employee devices. Conduct periodic audits to verify disposal procedures are followed consistently across the organization.

Implementation: CloudWatch logs track data access. S3 access logs provide disposal audit trail. KMS key usage logged via CloudTrail.

name: C1.2 The entity disposes of confidential information to meet the entity's objectives related to confidentiality.
description:
C1.2 (C1 - Confidentiality Criteria): The entity disposes of confidential information to meet the entity's objectives related to confidentiality.

Implement secure disposal procedures to ensure confidential information cannot be recovered after it's no longer needed. Establish clear triggers for disposal - end of retention period, project completion, contract termination, or explicit disposal request. Create procedures to identify all instances of confidential information scheduled for destruction, including primary copies, backups, archives, and copies on employee devices. For electronic data, use appropriate destruction methods based on sensitivity - simple deletion for low-risk data, secure overwriting for moderate risk, and physical destruction or cryptographic erasure for high-risk data. For physical documents, use cross-cut shredding or certified destruction services. Maintain detailed records of destruction including what was destroyed, when, how, by whom, and under what authority. Obtain certificates of destruction from third-party services. Verify destruction is complete by checking all storage locations including backup systems. Implement procedures to handle mixed media (like hard drives in copiers) and ensure destruction methods are appropriate for the medium. Regular audits verify disposal procedures are followed consistently. Consider regulatory requirements that may override normal disposal schedules.

Implementation: KMS enables cryptographic erasure for secure disposal. S3 lifecycle policies automate retention. Data retention policy defines disposal procedures.

name: CC1.1.1 Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards Documentation
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal Code of Conduct that articulates the ethical standards and behavioral expectations applicable to all personnel, including employees, contractors, and business partners. This document shall define acceptable conduct regarding integrity, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, and professional behavior. The Code of Conduct must be approved by leadership, communicated to all relevant parties, and made readily accessible. Given the remote work environment, the document shall address ethical considerations specific to distributed teams, including data handling outside traditional office settings and professional conduct in virtual communications.

Implementation: Code of Conduct covers ethics, integrity, confidentiality, remote work considerations.

name: CC1.1.2 Leadership Commitment and Tone at the Top
description:
Executive leadership shall demonstrate visible commitment to integrity and ethical values through documented communications, decision-making practices, and organizational governance. Leadership must formally endorse the Code of Conduct and ethical standards, communicate expectations through regular channels, and model appropriate behavior. For a small organization operating remotely, this includes leadership participation in ethics-related discussions during team meetings, documented responses to ethical concerns, and consistent enforcement of standards. Leadership shall conduct periodic reviews of ethical compliance and address any identified concerns promptly and consistently to reinforce the importance of ethical conduct throughout the organization.

Implementation: CEO signed Code of Conduct. Training certificates demonstrate commitment.

name: CC1.1.3 Ethics Training and Awareness Program
description:
The organization shall implement a training and awareness program to ensure all personnel understand their ethical obligations and the standards set forth in the Code of Conduct. Training shall be provided upon onboarding and on an annual basis thereafter. The program must cover key topics including integrity expectations, reporting mechanisms for ethical concerns, consequences of violations, and specific considerations for remote work environments. Training completion shall be tracked and documented, with remediation procedures for personnel who do not complete required training within established timeframes.

Implementation: Annual training completed Dec 9, 2025. Completion tracked via certificates.

name: CC1.1.4 Ethics Violation Reporting and Response Procedures
description:
The organization shall establish formal procedures for reporting suspected ethical violations and responding to such reports in a timely and consistent manner. A confidential reporting mechanism shall be made available to all personnel, enabling them to raise concerns without fear of retaliation. All reported concerns shall be documented, investigated appropriately, and resolved with documented outcomes. Disciplinary actions for confirmed violations shall be applied consistently in accordance with established policies. Given the small team size and remote environment, the organization shall ensure reporting channels maintain appropriate confidentiality while enabling effective investigation and resolution.

Implementation: Ethics violation log maintained. Zero violations in 2025. Reporting procedures documented.

name: CC1.1 The entity demonstrates a commitment to integrity and ethical values.
description:
CC1.1 (CC1 - Control Environment): The entity demonstrates a commitment to integrity and ethical values.

Your organization needs to establish and communicate clear expectations for ethical behavior throughout the company. This starts with leadership setting the right tone from the top - showing through actions that integrity matters. Create a code of conduct that defines expected behavior for employees, contractors, and business partners. Train everyone on these standards and make sure they understand them. Regularly evaluate whether people are following the rules through reviews, audits, or observations. When violations occur, address them quickly and consistently to show that ethics policies have teeth. Small companies can start simple but must cover all stakeholders who interact with their systems and data.

Implementation: Code of Conduct signed by all. Training: CEO 8hrs security, contractor 4hrs privacy. Zero violations 2025.

name: CC1.2.1 Designation of Independent Oversight Authority
description:
The organization shall formally designate an independent oversight authority responsible for governance of the security and compliance program. Given the company's size of 2-5 employees, this authority may be an external advisor, board member, or senior executive who maintains independence from day-to-day IT and security operations. The designated authority must possess or have access to relevant expertise in security, privacy, and technology matters. This designation shall be documented in writing, clearly articulating the scope of oversight responsibilities, reporting relationships, and the basis for determining independence from operational management.

Implementation: CEO provides oversight with external advisor consultation. Documented in org structure.

name: CC1.2.2 Periodic Independent Oversight Reviews
description:
The designated independent oversight authority shall conduct periodic reviews of the organization's internal control environment, security posture, and management's performance in executing control activities. These reviews shall occur at a frequency appropriate to the organization's risk profile, but no less than annually. The oversight authority shall document their review activities, findings, and any recommendations for improvement. Management shall be required to respond to identified deficiencies and report on remediation progress. Review sessions shall include examination of control effectiveness, security incidents, compliance status, and any material changes to the risk environment.

Implementation: Quarterly meetings review security posture, incidents, compliance. Q4 2025 documented.

name: CC1.2 The board of directors demonstrates independence from management and exercises oversight of the development an
description:
CC1.2 (CC1 - Control Environment): The board of directors demonstrates independence from management and exercises oversight of the development and performance of internal control.

Someone independent from day-to-day operations must oversee your security and compliance program. This oversight body needs to understand and accept their responsibilities for internal controls. They should have (or obtain through advisors) relevant expertise in security, privacy, and technology to ask probing questions and challenge management. For smaller companies, this might be an outside advisor, board member, or senior executive who isn't directly involved in IT operations. They need sufficient independence to objectively evaluate controls and management's performance. Consider bringing in specialized consultants if your board lacks technical security expertise. Regular oversight reviews should examine whether controls are working as intended.

Implementation: Q4 2025 management meeting reviewed compliance, security posture, control effectiveness.

name: CC1.3.1 Organizational Structure and Reporting Lines Documentation
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal documentation of its organizational structure, including clear reporting relationships and lines of authority. Given the company's small size and remote work environment, this documentation must explicitly define the hierarchy, decision-making authority levels, and communication channels. The structure shall account for all personnel regardless of geographic location and shall be reviewed annually or upon significant organizational changes. Documentation must clearly delineate who reports to whom and establish escalation paths for operational, security, and privacy matters.

Implementation: Reporting lines and hierarchy documented for remote team.

name: CC1.3.2 Authority Delegation and Segregation of Duties Framework
description:
The organization shall establish a formal framework defining decision-making authorities and responsibilities across all critical functions. This framework must specify approval thresholds for system access provisioning, change authorization, incident response decisions, and privacy-related determinations. Given the organization's size constraints, the framework shall implement compensating controls where traditional segregation of duties is not feasible, such as enhanced monitoring, management review, and audit trails. The framework must address vendor and third-party relationship management, clearly establishing responsibilities and interaction protocols with external parties.

Implementation: Job descriptions define responsibilities. IAM roles enforce technical access.
tasks: Job Description Go To Market Contractor

name: CC1.3 Management establishes structures, reporting lines, and appropriate authorities and responsibilities in the pu
description:
CC1.3 (CC1 - Control Environment): Management establishes structures, reporting lines, and appropriate authorities and responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.

Create clear organizational structures that show reporting relationships and define who has authority for what decisions. Consider all parts of your organization including subsidiaries, remote offices, and outsourced providers. Document who can approve system access, authorize changes, handle incidents, and make privacy decisions. Define responsibilities at appropriate levels - not everything needs CEO approval, but critical decisions shouldn't rest with junior staff. Ensure proper segregation of duties to prevent any one person from having too much control. When working with external parties like vendors or partners, clearly establish their responsibilities and how they interact with your organization. For privacy and security matters, ensure structures support compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.

Implementation: Org chart defines roles. Job descriptions specify security responsibilities.

name: CC1.4.1 Personnel Competency Requirements and Background Verification
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain documented competency requirements for all roles, with particular emphasis on positions involving security responsibilities. Given the company's small size (2-5 employees) and the nature of contractor relationships, the organization shall verify professional references and validate claimed qualifications prior to granting access to sensitive systems. For a remote technology company of this size, this includes defining core security competencies expected of all team members and ensuring appropriate training is completed before accessing production systems.

Implementation: Competency requirements documented in job descriptions. Professional references verified. Security training completed before production access. Training certificates dated Dec 9, 2025.

name: CC1.4.2 Security Training Program and Competency Development
description:
The organization shall implement a security awareness and training program that provides initial onboarding training on security policies and procedures, followed by ongoing education to maintain current knowledge of security practices. Given the organization's size and remote work environment, training shall address remote work security considerations, data protection responsibilities, and role-specific security requirements. The organization shall maintain training records demonstrating completion and shall periodically evaluate personnel competence, addressing identified gaps through additional training or mentoring. Succession planning considerations for critical roles shall be documented to ensure continuity of operations.

Implementation: Annual performance evaluations completed. Security responsibilities assessed.

name: CC1.4 The entity demonstrates a commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals in alignment with o
description:
CC1.4 (CC1 - Control Environment): The entity demonstrates a commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals in alignment with objectives.

Build and maintain a team with the skills needed to protect data and systems. Establish clear competency requirements for each role, especially those involving security responsibilities. Check backgrounds of employees and contractors before granting access to sensitive systems - the depth of checking should match the sensitivity of the role. Provide initial training on security policies and ongoing education to keep skills current. Evaluate competence regularly and address gaps through training, mentoring, or hiring. Have succession plans for critical roles so you're not scrambling if someone leaves suddenly. Consider the technical competency of vendors and their employees too. Maintain training records to demonstrate your commitment to competence. Small companies might start with basic security awareness but should expand training as they grow.

Implementation: Training completed: CEO 8hrs, contractor 4hrs. Certificates dated Dec 9, 2025.
