name: CC1.5.1 Security Responsibilities in Role Definitions
description:
The organization shall formally document security and compliance responsibilities within job descriptions, employment agreements, and role expectations for all personnel. Given the remote work environment and small team size, each team member's security accountabilities must be explicitly defined and communicated during onboarding and annually thereafter. This includes clear delineation of data handling responsibilities, access management duties, incident reporting obligations, and compliance requirements specific to each role.

Implementation: Security responsibilities documented in job descriptions and evaluations.

name: CC1.5.2 Performance Evaluation and Accountability Measures
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal process for evaluating personnel performance against security and compliance objectives. Performance assessments must incorporate security-related criteria, including adherence to policies, completion of required training, and contribution to the organization's security posture. A documented sanctions process shall be maintained for addressing non-compliance, ranging from remedial training to disciplinary action, applied consistently across all personnel. For a small remote team, this process should be proportionate and focused on improvement while maintaining clear consequences for willful violations.

Implementation: PropelAuth enforces MFA and session management. IAM credential report shows 100% MFA compliance. Annual performance evaluations assess security responsibilities.

name: CC1.5 The entity holds individuals accountable for their internal control responsibilities in the pursuit of objecti
description:
CC1.5 (CC1 - Control Environment): The entity holds individuals accountable for their internal control responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.

Create accountability for security and control responsibilities throughout your organization. Clearly communicate what's expected through job descriptions, policies, and regular reinforcement. Establish performance measures that include security and compliance responsibilities - make it clear these aren't optional extras. Set up incentives and rewards that encourage good security behavior while being careful not to create pressures that might lead to corner-cutting. Evaluate performance regularly, looking at both adherence to policies and achievement of security objectives. When people don't meet expectations, take appropriate action ranging from additional training to disciplinary measures. For privacy-related violations, have a defined sanctions process that's consistently applied. Balance accountability with reasonable expectations - don't create impossible standards that encourage workarounds.

Implementation: PropelAuth handles authentication with MFA enforcement. IAM enforces least privilege access. Quarterly access reviews documented in board meetings.

name: CC2.1.1 IT Asset Inventory Management
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a comprehensive inventory of all information technology assets utilized in business operations. This inventory must encompass hardware devices (including employee-owned devices used for work purposes), software applications, cloud services, and data repositories. Given the remote work environment, particular attention shall be paid to documenting assets located at employee residences and third-party vendor locations. The inventory shall be reviewed and updated at least annually to ensure accuracy and completeness. Each asset entry shall include, at minimum: asset identifier, description, owner, location, and criticality classification.

Implementation: IT assets documented via AWS CLI: 8 Lambdas, 1 DocumentDB cluster, S3 buckets, VPC. Annual review in Q4 board meeting.

name: CC2.1.2 Information Classification and Data Flow Documentation
description:
The organization shall implement a formal information classification scheme that categorizes all organizational data according to sensitivity levels (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted). Data flow documentation shall be created and maintained to illustrate how information traverses organizational systems, including transfers to and from remote employee environments and external service providers. Classification labels shall be applied consistently across all data repositories and communications. Personnel shall receive guidance on handling requirements for each classification level. This documentation shall be reviewed annually or upon significant changes to systems or business processes.

Implementation: Classification: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. Data flows documented.

name: CC2.1 The entity obtains or generates and uses relevant, quality information to support the functioning of internal
description:
CC2.1 (CC2 - Communication and Information): The entity obtains or generates and uses relevant, quality information to support the functioning of internal control.

Maintain comprehensive, accurate information about your systems and controls to support good decision-making. Start by identifying what information you need to manage security effectively. Document data flows showing how information moves through your systems. Create and maintain an inventory of all IT assets including hardware, software, and data repositories. Classify information by sensitivity level (public, internal, confidential, restricted) to apply appropriate protections. Track where data is stored, including data on employee devices or at vendor locations. Ensure the information you use for security decisions is timely, accurate, complete, and protected from tampering. Review information quality regularly - outdated asset inventories or incorrect data classifications can lead to security gaps. Small companies should start with basic inventories and build more sophisticated information management over time.

Implementation: Asset inventory via AWS CLI: Lambda functions, DocumentDB, S3 buckets. Classification policy defines handling.

name: CC2.2.1 Internal Security Communication Framework
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal framework for communicating security-related information to all personnel. This framework must define communication channels, frequency, and methods appropriate for a remote workforce. Given the organization's size, this may be consolidated into regular team communications but must ensure all personnel receive timely updates regarding security objectives, policy changes, control responsibilities, and their individual duties in maintaining the security posture. Communication methods shall be documented and consistently applied across the distributed team.

Implementation: Security updates via regular team communications. All personnel receive timely updates.

name: CC2.2.2 Security Awareness Training Program
description:
The organization shall implement and maintain a security awareness training program that educates all personnel on recognizing and responding to security threats. Training content must address the specific risks associated with remote work environments, including phishing, social engineering, secure handling of company data, and proper use of collaboration tools. Training shall be conducted upon hire and at least annually thereafter, with completion tracked and documented. For personnel handling personal information, training must include specific guidance on privacy requirements and proper data handling procedures.

Implementation: Training certificates document awareness program completion.

name: CC2.2.3 Incident and Concern Reporting Mechanisms
description:
The organization shall establish clear, accessible mechanisms for personnel to report system failures, security incidents, policy violations, and other concerns. Given the small team size and remote environment, reporting procedures must be straightforward and well-communicated. The organization shall maintain a non-punitive reporting culture that encourages prompt disclosure of issues. A confidential reporting channel shall be available for sensitive matters. All personnel must be informed of how to utilize these reporting mechanisms, and management shall ensure timely acknowledgment and response to all reports received.

Implementation: Incident reporting mechanisms documented. Non-punitive culture established.

name: CC2.2 The entity internally communicates information necessary to support the functioning of internal control.
description:
CC2.2 (CC2 - Communication and Information): The entity internally communicates information necessary to support the functioning of internal control.

Establish effective internal communication to ensure everyone understands and can fulfill their security responsibilities. Communicate control responsibilities clearly to all personnel, including what's expected and how to carry out their duties. Keep staff informed about security objectives and any changes to those objectives. Share information about how to report system failures, security incidents, and other concerns - make reporting easy and non-punitive. Implement security awareness training that teaches employees to recognize and respond to threats. Ensure communication flows both up and down - management needs to hear about problems, and staff need to understand priorities. Provide separate, confidential channels (like anonymous hotlines) for sensitive reports. Choose communication methods that fit your audience - technical details for IT staff, practical guidance for general users. For privacy programs, include specific training on handling personal information properly.

Implementation: Security policy communicated to all. Annual training provided. Reporting procedures documented.

name: CC2.3.1 External Security Communication Framework
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal communication channels and documentation for conveying security-related information to external parties. This includes the publication of a comprehensive privacy notice on the company website, maintenance of security documentation for customer inquiries, and establishment of vendor security requirements. All external-facing security communications shall be reviewed and approved by appropriate personnel prior to publication or distribution.

Implementation: Privacy notice on website. Security docs available for customer inquiries.

name: CC2.3.2 External Security Reporting Mechanism
description:
The organization shall provide and maintain accessible mechanisms for external parties to report security concerns, vulnerabilities, or incidents. This includes establishing a dedicated security contact point (e.g., security@company.com), publishing responsible disclosure guidelines where appropriate, and implementing procedures for timely acknowledgment and response to external security reports. All reported concerns shall be documented, triaged, and addressed in accordance with established incident response procedures.

Implementation: DPA template defines vendor communication. Security reporting mechanisms established.
policies: Privacy Notice and Data Processing Agreement Template

name: CC2.3 The entity communicates with external parties regarding matters affecting the functioning of internal control.
description:
CC2.3 (CC2 - Communication and Information): The entity communicates with external parties regarding matters affecting the functioning of internal control.

Communicate appropriately with customers, vendors, regulators, and other external parties about your security practices. This includes publishing privacy notices, sharing security requirements with vendors, responding to customer security inquiries, and providing ways for external parties to report security concerns or incidents.

Implementation: Privacy notice published. Security contact established. Vendor requirements in contracts.

name: CC3.1.1 Security Program Objectives Documentation
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal document that articulates the security program objectives with sufficient clarity and specificity. This document shall define the organization's goals for protecting customer data, maintaining system availability, ensuring processing integrity, safeguarding confidential information, and respecting privacy rights. The objectives shall be aligned with business operations, regulatory requirements, and stakeholder expectations. Given the organization's remote work environment, objectives shall specifically address distributed workforce security considerations. The document shall be reviewed and approved by leadership annually or upon significant changes to the business environment.

Implementation: Security objectives aligned with business ops, regulatory requirements, stakeholder needs. Humadroid risk register documents 6 risks across categories.

name: CC3.1.2 Risk Identification Framework Based on Defined Objectives
description:
The organization shall implement a structured approach to identify and assess risks that could impede the achievement of documented security objectives. This framework shall enable systematic identification of threats and vulnerabilities across all Trust Services Criteria domains relevant to the organization's operations. The risk identification process shall consider the unique risk profile associated with a fully remote technology organization, including distributed access points, cloud infrastructure dependencies, and remote collaboration tools. Risk assessments shall be conducted at least annually and upon material changes to systems, processes, or the operating environment.

Implementation: Security Hub identifies vulnerabilities. Risk procedure defines assessment approach. Humadroid tracks risks by category with severity scoring.

name: CC3.1 The entity specifies objectives with sufficient clarity to enable identification and assessment of risks.
description:
CC3.1 (CC3 - Risk Assessment): The entity specifies objectives with sufficient clarity to enable identification and assessment of risks.

Define clear goals for what you're trying to protect and achieve with your security program. These objectives should cover protecting customer data, maintaining system availability, ensuring accurate processing, keeping confidential information secret, and respecting privacy rights. Clear objectives help you identify what could go wrong and where to focus your security efforts.

Implementation: Risk assessment procedure documents objectives and identification methodology. Humadroid risk register tracks 6 identified risks across categories.

name: CC3.2.1 Enterprise Risk Assessment Framework
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal risk assessment framework that identifies, analyzes, and evaluates risks to the achievement of business objectives. This framework shall encompass enterprise-wide risks as well as risks specific to systems, processes, and operations. The assessment shall consider both internal factors (personnel errors, system failures, process deficiencies) and external factors (cyber threats, natural disasters, regulatory changes). Risk assessments shall be conducted at least annually or upon significant changes to the business environment, with appropriate management involvement to ensure business context is properly considered in risk tolerance decisions.

Implementation: Framework covers enterprise, system, and process risks. Internal and external factors. Humadroid risk scoring uses Multi-Impact Assessment method.

name: CC3.2.2 Third-Party and Vendor Risk Evaluation
description:
The organization shall identify and assess risks arising from vendors, business partners, and other third parties with access to organizational systems or data. This evaluation shall be integrated into the overall risk assessment process and shall consider the nature and extent of third-party access, the sensitivity of data or systems involved, and the potential impact of third-party failures or breaches. Risk treatment decisions for third-party relationships shall be documented and reviewed periodically to ensure continued appropriateness as business relationships evolve.

Implementation: Humadroid tracks 2 vendors (AWS and PropelAuth) with risk tier assignments. SOC 2 compliance verified via vendor assessments.

name: CC3.2 The entity identifies risks to the achievement of its objectives and analyzes risks as a basis for determining
description:
CC3.2 (CC3 - Risk Assessment): The entity identifies risks to the achievement of its objectives and analyzes risks as a basis for determining how the risks should be managed.

Conduct comprehensive risk assessments covering all levels of your organization - from enterprise-wide risks down to specific systems and processes. Consider both internal factors (employee errors, system failures, process gaps) and external factors (hackers, natural disasters, regulatory changes). Identify specific threats to your objectives and the vulnerabilities that could be exploited. Pay special attention to risks from vendors, business partners, and other third parties with system access. Involve appropriate management levels in risk assessment - they understand business context and can make informed decisions about risk tolerance. Estimate the likelihood and potential impact of each risk to prioritize your response. Decide how to handle each risk: accept it (if impact is low), avoid it (stop the risky activity), reduce it (implement controls), or transfer it (through insurance or contracts). Document your risk assessment process and review it regularly as threats evolve.

Implementation: Annual risk assessments with management involvement. Likelihood and impact evaluated. Humadroid risk detail shows probability/impact scoring (e.g. 4/3 = score 32).

name: CC3.3.1 Fraud Risk Assessment and Documentation
description:
The organization shall conduct and document a formal fraud risk assessment that identifies potential fraud scenarios relevant to its operations. This assessment must evaluate the fraud triangle elements (incentive/pressure, opportunity, and rationalization) for both internal and external threat actors. Given the remote work environment, particular attention shall be given to risks associated with distributed access to systems, data exfiltration opportunities, and the reduced oversight inherent in remote operations. The assessment shall be reviewed and updated annually or upon significant organizational changes.

Implementation: Fraud triangle evaluated. Humadroid risk detail shows treatment strategy (Mitigate) for People Risk with documented treatment actions.

name: CC3.3.2 Fraud Prevention Controls and Monitoring
description:
The organization shall implement and maintain controls designed to prevent and detect fraudulent activities, including unauthorized system modifications, data theft, asset misappropriation, and falsification of records. For a technology company of this size operating remotely, controls shall include segregation of duties where practicable, access logging and review procedures, and mechanisms for reporting suspected fraudulent activity. Management shall establish clear accountability for fraud prevention oversight and ensure all personnel understand their responsibilities in maintaining the integrity of organizational systems and data.

Implementation: GuardDuty monitors for unauthorized access patterns. Security Hub aggregates findings. CloudTrail logs all API activity for fraud detection.

name: CC3.3 The entity considers the potential for fraud in assessing risks.
description:
CC3.3 (CC3 - Risk Assessment): The entity considers the potential for fraud in assessing risks.

Think about how someone might intentionally misuse their access or manipulate your systems for personal gain. Consider both external threats and insider risks, including theft of data or assets, unauthorized system changes, and falsification of records. Look at what might motivate fraud, what opportunities exist, and how someone might justify their actions.

Implementation: Fraud risk in assessment procedure. Humadroid risk register includes People Risk category addressing insider threats.

name: CC3.4.1 Change Identification and Monitoring Process
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal process for identifying and monitoring changes that could significantly impact the system of internal control. This process shall encompass monitoring of regulatory and compliance landscape changes, business operational changes including growth or restructuring, technology infrastructure and application modifications, personnel changes particularly in key security and compliance roles, third-party vendor relationships and service provider changes, and emerging threat intelligence relevant to the organization's technology sector. Given the organization's small team size and remote work environment, this process shall be streamlined yet comprehensive, with designated responsibility for change monitoring assigned to appropriate personnel.

Implementation: Security Hub monitors configuration changes and new vulnerabilities.

name: CC3.4.2 Change Impact Assessment and Control Adequacy Review
description:
The organization shall implement a structured methodology for assessing the impact of identified changes on the existing risk profile and evaluating whether current internal controls remain adequate. For each significant change identified, the organization shall conduct a documented impact assessment that evaluates the effect on existing risks, identifies new risks introduced by the change, determines whether existing controls sufficiently address modified or new risks, and recommends control modifications or new controls as necessary. Assessment frequency shall be commensurate with the pace of change, with immediate assessment triggered for material changes and periodic reviews conducted at minimum on a quarterly basis. Given the organization's remote work environment, particular attention shall be given to changes affecting remote access, collaboration tools, and distributed workforce security controls.

Implementation: Change triggers documented. Quarterly minimum review cadence.

name: CC3.4 The entity identifies and assesses changes that could significantly impact the system of internal control.
description:
CC3.4 (CC3 - Risk Assessment): The entity identifies and assesses changes that could significantly impact the system of internal control.

Stay alert to changes that could affect your security posture - new regulations, business growth, technology updates, staff turnover, new vendors, or emerging threats. Have a process to evaluate how these changes impact your risks and whether your existing controls are still adequate. Regular assessment helps prevent security gaps during transitions.

Implementation: Security Hub monitors for significant changes. Humadroid Q4 2025 risk snapshot captures quarterly risk assessment updates.

name: CC4.1.1 Internal Control Monitoring Program
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal program for ongoing monitoring of internal controls. This program shall define the scope of controls subject to evaluation, assign responsibility for monitoring activities, and establish a risk-based schedule for assessments. Given the organization's size, monitoring activities should be streamlined yet comprehensive, with clear ownership assigned to designated personnel. The program shall include both continuous monitoring mechanisms (such as automated alerts and log reviews) and periodic assessments appropriate to the organization's risk profile.

Implementation: CloudWatch: automated alerts, log reviews. Continuous and periodic assessments.
policies: Penetration Testing and Security Assessment Procedure

name: CC4.1.2 Security Control Testing and Evaluation
description:
The organization shall conduct periodic testing and evaluation of security controls to verify their operational effectiveness. Testing activities shall include, at minimum, annual vulnerability assessments via automated scanning tools, annual access log reviews, and periodic verification of critical security configurations. For a remote work environment, particular attention shall be given to evaluating controls related to remote access, endpoint security, and cloud service configurations. Deficiencies identified through testing shall be documented, prioritized based on risk, and remediated within established timeframes.

Implementation: Security Hub + Dependabot provide continuous vulnerability scanning (21 alerts tracked). GuardDuty for runtime threat detection. Annual access review in Q4 board meeting.
policies: Penetration Testing and Security Assessment Procedure

name: CC4.1 The entity selects, develops, and performs ongoing evaluations to ascertain whether the components of internal
description:
CC4.1 (CC4 - Monitoring Activities): The entity selects, develops, and performs ongoing evaluations to ascertain whether the components of internal control are present and functioning.

Regularly check that your security controls actually work as intended. This includes routine monitoring like reviewing access logs, as well as periodic assessments like penetration tests or compliance audits. Choose evaluation methods that match your risk level - high-risk areas need more frequent and thorough testing.

Implementation: CloudWatch, GuardDuty, Security Hub provide continuous monitoring. accessReview Lambda for periodic reviews.
policies: Penetration Testing and Security Assessment Procedure

name: CC4.2.1 Internal Control Deficiency Documentation and Tracking
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a formal process for documenting, categorizing, and tracking internal control deficiencies from identification through remediation. All identified security weaknesses and control gaps must be recorded in a centralized tracking system with appropriate severity classifications, assigned ownership, and target remediation dates. The tracking mechanism shall capture the nature of the deficiency, potential impact, root cause analysis, and corrective action plans. Given the organization's size, a streamlined approach utilizing existing project management or issue tracking tools is acceptable, provided all requisite information is captured and maintained.

Implementation: Findings documented with severity classification, ownership, remediation dates.

name: CC4.2.2 Deficiency Communication and Escalation Procedures
description:
The organization shall implement formal communication and escalation procedures to ensure internal control deficiencies are reported to appropriate parties in a timely manner commensurate with their severity. Critical and high-severity deficiencies must be escalated to senior management within defined timeframes. Regular status reporting on the overall state of the security program and outstanding deficiencies shall be provided to leadership. For an organization of this size operating in a remote environment, communication protocols should leverage established digital communication channels while ensuring appropriate documentation of all escalations and management acknowledgments.

Implementation: CloudWatch logs retained for investigation. Escalation via established channels.

name: CC4.2 The entity evaluates and communicates internal control deficiencies in a timely manner to those parties respon
description:
CC4.2 (CC4 - Monitoring Activities): The entity evaluates and communicates internal control deficiencies in a timely manner to those parties responsible for taking corrective action.

When security weaknesses are found, document them clearly, communicate them to the right people, and track them until they're fixed. Ensure serious issues escalate to senior management quickly, and keep leadership informed about the overall state of your security program. Learn from deficiencies to prevent similar issues in the future.

Implementation: Security Hub identifies deficiencies. CloudWatch logs support investigation.

name: CC5.1.1 Risk-Based Control Selection and Documentation
description:
The organization shall maintain a formal process for selecting and documenting security controls based on identified risks. Control selection must demonstrate clear alignment between specific risks and chosen mitigations, with documented rationale for each control's inclusion. The selection process shall consider cost-effectiveness, operational impact, and the organization's remote work environment. A control inventory shall be maintained that maps each control to its corresponding risk(s) and categorizes controls as preventive or detective, and technical or procedural.

Implementation: IAM roles and KMS encryption implement preventive access and data controls.

name: CC5.1.2 Balanced Control Framework Implementation
description:
The organization shall implement a balanced portfolio of security controls that includes both preventive measures (such as access restrictions, encryption, and authentication requirements) and detective measures (such as logging, monitoring, and periodic reviews). Given the remote work environment, particular emphasis shall be placed on controls that address distributed workforce risks. The control framework shall ensure adequate coverage across technical safeguards (automated systems and tools) and procedural safeguards (policies, training, and manual processes) appropriate for a small technology organization.

Implementation: GuardDuty provides threat detection. CloudWatch provides continuous monitoring with alarms. Security Hub aggregates security findings for detective controls.

name: CC5.1 The entity selects and develops control activities that contribute to the mitigation of risks to the achieveme
description:
CC5.1 (CC5 - Control Activities): The entity selects and develops control activities that contribute to the mitigation of risks to the achievement of objectives to acceptable levels.

Choose security controls that effectively address your identified risks without being overly complex or expensive. Mix preventive controls (like access restrictions) with detective controls (like monitoring), and ensure you have both technical and procedural safeguards. Focus on controls that give you the best risk reduction for your investment.

Implementation: Balanced controls: Preventive (IAM, KMS), Detective (CloudWatch, GuardDuty), Corrective (Lambda, IR).

name: CC5.2.1 IT Infrastructure and Access Management
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal controls over IT infrastructure and administrative access. This includes implementing role-based access controls for all critical systems, maintaining an inventory of IT assets, restricting administrative privileges to authorized personnel only, and ensuring secure configuration of network infrastructure. Given the remote work environment, particular attention shall be paid to secure remote access mechanisms and endpoint security controls.

Implementation: CloudFormation templates ensure consistent, version-controlled deployments.

name: CC5.2.2 Change Management and Software Development Controls
description:
The organization shall implement formal change management procedures governing modifications to IT systems, applications, and infrastructure. All changes shall be documented, reviewed, tested, and approved prior to implementation in production environments. For a technology company of this size, this includes establishing separation of duties where feasible, maintaining version control for all code and configurations, and ensuring changes are traceable and reversible. Emergency change procedures shall be documented for time-sensitive situations.

Implementation: Branch protection: PR approval required before merge.

name: CC5.2.3 Technology Acquisition and Security Assessment
description:
The organization shall establish procedures to ensure that technology acquisitions, including software, hardware, and cloud services, meet defined security requirements prior to deployment. This includes conducting security assessments of new vendors and technologies, reviewing security certifications and compliance attestations, and ensuring contractual provisions address security obligations. Given the company's technology industry context, particular scrutiny shall be applied to third-party components and dependencies.

Implementation: Technology acquisition requires security assessment before deployment.

name: CC5.2 The entity selects and develops general control activities over technology to support the achievement of objec
description:
CC5.2 (CC5 - Control Activities): The entity selects and develops general control activities over technology to support the achievement of objectives.

Implement fundamental IT controls that support all your systems and applications. This includes managing IT infrastructure, controlling software changes, restricting administrative access, maintaining system configurations, and ensuring technology acquisitions meet security requirements. These foundational controls support everything else you do.

Implementation: IaC via CloudFormation. GitHub branch protection enforces code review.

name: CC5.3.1 Security Policy Documentation and Procedural Framework
description:
The organization shall maintain a formal framework that translates approved security policies into documented operational procedures. Each policy shall have corresponding step-by-step procedures that specify the actions required for implementation, the personnel responsible for execution, and the timelines for completion of critical tasks. Procedures shall be written in clear, actionable language appropriate for the intended audience and shall be readily accessible to all relevant personnel through the organization's document management system.

Implementation: Step-by-step procedures: access provisioning, change requests, incident reporting.

name: CC5.3.2 Control Activity Competency and Authorization
description:
The organization shall ensure that personnel assigned to execute control activities possess the requisite skills, knowledge, and formal authorization to perform their designated responsibilities. This includes maintaining documentation of role assignments, ensuring appropriate training has been completed, and verifying that personnel have been granted the necessary system access and decision-making authority. Given the organization's remote work environment, particular attention shall be given to ensuring personnel can effectively execute controls independent of physical location.

Implementation: Role competencies in job descriptions. Training verifies. IAM grants access.

name: CC5.3.3 Periodic Review of Control Procedures
description:
The organization shall establish a formal review cycle to assess the continued relevance and effectiveness of documented procedures. Reviews shall be conducted at least annually, or more frequently when significant changes occur to the business environment, technology infrastructure, or regulatory requirements. The review process shall evaluate whether procedures remain aligned with current policies, reflect actual operational practices, and adequately address evolving risks. Findings from reviews shall be documented and result in timely updates to affected procedures.

Implementation: Annual policy review documented in Q4 2025 board meeting. Updates based on risk assessment findings. Next review scheduled Q4 2026.

name: CC5.3 The entity deploys control activities through policies that establish what is expected and in procedures that
description:
CC5.3 (CC5 - Control Activities): The entity deploys control activities through policies that establish what is expected and in procedures that put policies into action.

Turn your security policies into practical procedures that people can actually follow. Document step-by-step processes, assign clear responsibilities, set timelines for critical tasks, ensure staff have the skills and authority to perform controls, and regularly review whether procedures still make sense as your business evolves.

Implementation: Policies translated to procedures: access control, change management, incident response.

name: CC6.1.1 Information Asset Inventory and Classification
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain a comprehensive inventory of all information assets requiring protection, including infrastructure components, software applications, and data repositories. Each asset shall be classified according to its sensitivity and criticality to business operations. This inventory shall be reviewed and updated at least annually to ensure accuracy and completeness. Asset classification shall inform the application of appropriate security controls and access restrictions.

Implementation: PropelAuth manages user access inventory. IAM credential report: 100% MFA compliance. Annual asset review in Q4 board meeting.

name: CC6.1.2 Logical Access Control Implementation
description:
The organization shall implement logical access controls to restrict system and data access based on the principle of least privilege and role-based access requirements. Access control software and configurations shall enforce authentication requirements prior to granting access to protected resources. Multi-factor authentication shall be required for all remote access, administrative functions, and access to sensitive data. Access rules shall be documented and aligned with data classification levels and approved user roles.

Implementation: PropelAuth + IAM password policy: 14+ chars, complexity, 90-day rotation.

name: CC6.1.3 Network Security and Segmentation
description:
The organization shall implement network security controls to protect information assets from unauthorized access and security threats. Given the remote work environment, all network communications shall be secured through appropriate encryption and access controls. Network architecture shall incorporate segmentation or zero-trust principles to limit the potential impact of security incidents. All access points, including APIs and remote connections, shall be identified, documented, and secured with appropriate controls.

Implementation: VPC with private subnets. Security groups and NACLs filter traffic.

name: CC6.1.4 Encryption and Key Management
description:
The organization shall implement encryption controls to protect sensitive data at rest, in transit, and during processing as appropriate to the risk level. Encryption methods shall be selected based on industry standards and the sensitivity of the data being protected. A formal key management program shall be established to govern the entire lifecycle of cryptographic keys, including generation, storage, distribution, use, rotation, and destruction. Key management procedures shall ensure keys are protected from unauthorized access and disclosure.

Implementation: KMS: 8 keys with rotation. S3 100% encrypted. DocumentDB encrypted.

name: CC6.1.5 Credential and Authentication Management
description:
The organization shall establish formal procedures for managing credentials for both user accounts and system/service accounts. Password policies shall enforce complexity, length, and rotation requirements appropriate to the access level granted. Service account credentials shall be secured, documented, and subject to periodic review. Authentication mechanisms shall be configured to protect against common attack vectors including brute force attempts and credential stuffing.

Implementation: IAM roles: least privilege. Users get only required permissions.

name: CC6.1 The entity implements logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures over protected infor
description:
CC6.1 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity implements logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures over protected information assets to protect them from security threats.

Implement comprehensive technical controls to protect your information assets from unauthorized access. Start with a complete inventory of what needs protection - infrastructure, software, and data. Evaluate new system architectures for security before implementation. Use access control software and configuration standards to restrict logical access appropriately. Implement strong authentication, requiring users and systems to prove their identity before accessing resources - use multi-factor authentication for sensitive access. Consider network segmentation or zero-trust architectures to limit the blast radius of any breach. Manage all access points including APIs and remote connections. Establish access rules based on data classification and user roles. Properly manage credentials for both people and system accounts. Encrypt sensitive data at rest, in transit, and during processing when appropriate. Protect encryption keys through their entire lifecycle - generation, storage, use, and destruction. Choose encryption methods appropriate to your risk level.

Implementation: PropelAuth for app auth. IAM for AWS. MFA required. Strong password policy.

name: CC6.2.1 User Access Request and Authorization Process
description:
The organization shall maintain a formal, documented process for requesting and authorizing system access for all internal and external users. Prior to provisioning any system credentials, a written or electronic access request must be submitted specifying the user's identity, role, business justification, and required access levels. All access requests shall be reviewed and approved by an appropriate authority (e.g., department head, system owner, or designated manager) before credentials are issued. The approval process must verify that the requested access aligns with the user's job responsibilities and adheres to the principle of least privilege.

Implementation: PropelAuth manages user registration. CEO approval required before access granted (documented in access policy). Least privilege enforced via role assignment.

name: CC6.2.2 User Account Lifecycle Management and Periodic Review
description:
The organization shall implement controls to manage the complete lifecycle of user accounts, including registration, modification, and timely deactivation. A centralized inventory of all user accounts shall be maintained, documenting the user's identity, access privileges, and account status. Access reviews shall be conducted at least annually to verify that all accounts remain necessary and appropriate for users' current roles. Upon termination of employment or change in role, access shall be modified or revoked within one business day. The organization shall maintain documented procedures for offboarding that ensure prompt credential revocation across all systems.

Implementation: PropelAuth centralizes user inventory. IAM enforces MFA (100% compliance). Annual access review documented in Q4 2025 board meeting. Offboarding procedure in access policy.

name: CC6.2 Prior to issuing system credentials and granting system access, the entity registers and authorizes new intern
description:
CC6.2 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): Prior to issuing system credentials and granting system access, the entity registers and authorizes new internal and external users whose access is administered by the entity.

Before giving anyone access to your systems, verify they're authorized and need that access for their job. Create a formal process for requesting, approving, and setting up new accounts. Regularly review all accounts to ensure they're still needed and immediately disable access when someone leaves or changes roles.

Implementation: PropelAuth handles registration and auth. IAM enforces MFA. Strong passwords.

name: CC6.3.1 Role-Based Access Control Framework
description:
Establish and maintain a documented role-based access control (RBAC) framework that defines access permissions for each role within the organization. Given the small team size, document the specific access rights required for each team member's responsibilities across all systems, applications, and data repositories. Maintain an access matrix that clearly maps roles to permitted resources and access levels. This framework shall serve as the authoritative reference for granting, modifying, and revoking access privileges.

Implementation: Roles map to specific resources and access levels.

name: CC6.3.2 Access Authorization and Change Management
description:
Implement formal procedures for authorizing, modifying, and removing access to organizational systems and data. All access requests and changes must be documented and approved by an appropriate authority prior to implementation. For this organization's size, the founder or designated lead shall approve all access changes. Maintain audit trails of all access provisioning activities, including the requestor, approver, date, and specific access granted or revoked. Ensure timely removal of access upon role changes or employment termination.

Implementation: Access changes require CEO approval. CloudTrail logs all IAM changes. PropelAuth logs user provisioning. Timely revocation: access removed within 1 business day of termination.

name: CC6.3.3 Segregation of Duties Controls
description:
Identify and document incompatible functions that must be segregated to prevent fraud and errors. Given the organization's small size where complete segregation may not be feasible, implement compensating controls such as enhanced monitoring, detailed audit logging, and periodic independent review of sensitive transactions. At minimum, ensure that critical functions such as payment initiation and approval, code deployment and review, and administrative access changes involve oversight from more than one individual where possible.

Implementation: Compensating controls: monitoring, logging, periodic review where segregation limited.

name: CC6.3 The entity authorizes, modifies, or removes access to data, software, functions, and other protected informati
description:
CC6.3 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity authorizes, modifies, or removes access to data, software, functions, and other protected information assets based on roles and responsibilities.

Grant people only the minimum access they need to do their jobs, and separate conflicting duties so no single person can commit fraud undetected. Document what access each role should have, require approval for access changes, regularly review whether access is still appropriate, and ensure incompatible functions (like requesting and approving payments) are separated.

Implementation: PropelAuth roles define access. IAM roles enforce AWS permissions.

name: CC6.4.1 Cloud Infrastructure Physical Security Assurance
description:
As a fully remote organization utilizing cloud infrastructure, the entity shall maintain documented assurance that all cloud service providers and data center facilities housing company data implement appropriate physical security controls. This includes obtaining and reviewing SOC 2 reports or equivalent attestations from cloud providers, maintaining an inventory of all third-party facilities where company data resides, and ensuring contractual requirements for physical security are in place. The entity shall verify that providers implement access controls, environmental protections, and visitor management procedures commensurate with the sensitivity of data stored.

Implementation: AWS: access controls, environmental protections, 24/7 security. SOC 2 report reviewed.

name: CC6.4.2 Remote Employee Equipment and Media Security
description:
The entity shall establish and enforce policies governing the physical security of company-owned equipment and any media containing sensitive information at remote work locations. Employees shall be required to implement reasonable physical safeguards for laptops, mobile devices, and any physical media containing company data. This includes secure storage when not in use, prohibition of leaving devices unattended in public spaces, and proper handling and destruction of any physical documents or media containing sensitive information. The policy shall address equipment return procedures upon termination and reporting requirements for lost or stolen devices.

Implementation: Remote equipment: device encryption (FileVault), secure storage, 24hr lost device reporting.

name: CC6.4 The entity restricts physical access to facilities and protected information assets.
description:
CC6.4 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity restricts physical access to facilities and protected information assets.

Control who can physically access your servers, network equipment, backup media, and paper records containing sensitive information. Use locks, badges, or keys to restrict access, maintain logs of who enters secure areas, escort visitors, and promptly revoke physical access when no longer needed. Even small offices need basic physical security for IT equipment.

Implementation: Fully remote org. AWS SOC 2 certified data centers provide physical security.

name: CC6.5.1 Data Sanitization and Media Destruction Procedures
description:
The organization shall establish and maintain formal procedures for the secure sanitization and destruction of data storage media prior to disposal, reuse, or transfer. Given the remote work environment, these procedures must address both company-owned and employee-owned devices that may contain company data. Procedures shall specify approved methods for data wiping (using industry-standard tools meeting NIST 800-88 guidelines) and physical destruction requirements for media that cannot be adequately sanitized. The procedures must also address the secure disposal of paper documents containing sensitive information through shredding or secure destruction services.

Implementation: KMS for cloud data. Secure deletion for S3. NIST 800-88 guidelines.

name: CC6.5.2 Asset Disposal Verification and Documentation
description:
The organization shall implement a verification process to confirm that all sensitive information has been removed from assets before discontinuing logical and physical protections. This includes maintaining an inventory of assets pending disposal, documenting the chain of custody during the disposal process, and retaining destruction records for audit purposes. For the remote workforce, this process must include procedures for employees to return or certify the sanitization of company data from devices used for work purposes, including laptops, mobile devices, and removable storage media.

Implementation: KMS key deletion enables cryptographic erasure verification. CloudWatch logs track data access and deletion. S3 access logs provide disposal audit trail.

name: CC6.5 The entity discontinues logical and physical protections over assets only after the removal of all sensitive i
description:
CC6.5 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity discontinues logical and physical protections over assets only after the removal of all sensitive information from the assets.

Before disposing of computers, drives, phones, or paper documents, ensure data cannot be recovered by others. Wipe or physically destroy storage media, shred sensitive documents, and remove company data from employee devices before reuse or disposal. Keep records of destruction for sensitive data to prove proper disposal.

Implementation: KMS cryptographic erasure. S3 lifecycle automates deletion. Retention policy defines triggers.

name: CC6.6.1 Network Perimeter Security Controls
description:
The organization shall implement and maintain network perimeter security controls to protect against external threats. Given the remote work environment, this includes cloud-based firewall solutions, secure DNS filtering, and network segmentation for any cloud infrastructure. All external-facing services must be protected by appropriate security controls, with unnecessary ports and services disabled. Security configurations shall be documented and reviewed periodically to ensure alignment with current threat landscape.

Implementation: VPC + private subnets isolate infrastructure. Security groups control access.
policies: API Security and Rate Limiting Standard

name: CC6.6.2 Secure Remote Access Management
description:
The organization shall establish secure remote access mechanisms for all personnel accessing company systems. Given the fully cloud-based architecture, the organization implements a zero-trust approach where all access requires authentication via PropelAuth with MFA, regardless of network location. Access is granted based on the principle of least privilege through IAM roles, and all access sessions are logged via CloudTrail and application audit logs. This approach provides equivalent or better security than traditional VPN for a cloud-native organization.

Implementation: Zero-trust model: PropelAuth + MFA required for all access. No VPN needed - all services cloud-hosted. IAM enforces least privilege. CloudTrail + CloudWatch log all access.
policies: API Security and Rate Limiting Standard

name: CC6.6.3 Threat Detection and Security Monitoring
description:
The organization shall deploy and maintain threat detection capabilities to identify and respond to external threats. This includes intrusion detection or prevention systems, security monitoring tools, and alerting mechanisms for suspicious activities. Security tools shall be configured to detect current threat patterns and updated regularly to address emerging threats. Alerts shall be reviewed promptly, and significant security events shall be escalated according to established procedures.

Implementation: Security groups + CloudWatch alarms for threat detection and alerting.
policies: API Security and Rate Limiting Standard

name: CC6.6 The entity implements logical access security measures to protect against threats from sources outside its sys
description:
CC6.6 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity implements logical access security measures to protect against threats from sources outside its system boundaries.

Protect your network perimeter from external threats using firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and secure remote access methods like VPNs. Monitor and restrict what can connect to your network from the internet, require extra authentication for external access, and keep security tools updated to detect new threats.

Implementation: Security groups restrict traffic. NACLs provide defense in depth. No public DB access.
policies: API Security and Rate Limiting Standard

name: CC6.7.1 Data Transmission Encryption Standards
description:
The organization shall implement and enforce encryption standards for all sensitive data transmitted across networks. This includes mandatory TLS 1.2 or higher for web communications, encrypted email protocols, and secure API connections. All remote work communications must traverse encrypted channels, and VPN or zero-trust network access shall be required for accessing internal systems from external locations.

Implementation: Lambda HTTPS-only. PropelAuth manages API keys.
policies: API Security and Rate Limiting Standard

name: CC6.7.2 Removable Media and Data Transfer Controls
description:
The organization shall establish formal controls governing external data transfers. Given the fully remote, cloud-first work environment where company data resides entirely in cloud services (AWS, PropelAuth), controls focus on securing cloud access rather than removable media. Approved secure methods shall be designated for sensitive document exchange, with appropriate access controls enforced via IAM and PropelAuth roles.

Implementation: Cloud-first architecture: all data in AWS (DocumentDB, S3). No on-premise data requiring USB transfers. PropelAuth + IAM enforce access controls. TLS 1.2+ for all data in transit.
policies: API Security and Rate Limiting Standard

name: CC6.7.3 Mobile Device Data Protection
description:
The organization shall implement controls to protect company data accessed from remote devices. Given the small team size and remote work environment, this includes mandatory device encryption (FileVault for macOS), strong authentication via PropelAuth with MFA, and session management controls. For a company of this size, centralized mobile device management (MDM) is not required; instead, security is enforced through encryption, authentication, and access controls at the application layer.

Implementation: FileVault encryption on all macOS devices. PropelAuth enforces MFA for application access. Session timeout configured. 24-hour lost device reporting requirement in security policy.
policies: API Security and Rate Limiting Standard

name: CC6.7.4 Unauthorized Data Transfer Monitoring
description:
The organization shall implement monitoring mechanisms to detect and alert on unauthorized data transfers or anomalous data movement patterns. This includes monitoring of cloud application usage, large file transfers, and access to sensitive data repositories. Alerts shall be reviewed promptly, and suspected unauthorized transfers shall be investigated and documented.

Implementation: DocumentDB TLS required. CloudWatch monitors data access patterns.
policies: API Security and Rate Limiting Standard

name: CC6.7 The entity restricts the transmission, movement, and removal of information to authorized internal and externa
description:
CC6.7 (CC6 - Logical and Physical Access Controls): The entity restricts the transmission, movement, and removal of information to authorized internal and external users and processes.

Control and protect data when it moves outside your direct control. Use encryption for sensitive data in transit, restrict the use of removable media like USB drives, implement secure file sharing instead of email for sensitive documents, and protect mobile devices that access company data. Monitor for unauthorized data transfers.

Implementation: TLS 1.2+ for all transit. Zero-trust via PropelAuth. HTTPS-only endpoints.

name: CC6.8.1 Endpoint Protection and Antivirus Management
description:
The organization shall maintain endpoint protection capabilities across company-managed devices. For a small remote team using macOS devices, this includes reliance on built-in macOS security features (XProtect, Gatekeeper, MRT) supplemented by cloud-based scanning of code and containers. Given the organization's size and remote work environment, endpoint protection focuses on secure device configuration, encryption, and cloud-native security tools rather than traditional enterprise endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions.

Implementation: macOS XProtect/Gatekeeper provide endpoint protection. FileVault encryption enabled. ECR scans containers. Dependabot scans code dependencies. Security Hub aggregates findings.

name: CC6.8.2 Software Installation Controls and Patch Management
description:
The organization shall establish controls governing software installation and maintain current patch levels across all systems. Administrative privileges for software installation shall be restricted to authorized personnel only. A documented process shall exist for evaluating, approving, and deploying software updates and security patches in a timely manner. For the remote workforce, this includes ensuring personal devices used for work purposes comply with minimum security requirements.

Implementation: Dependabot auto-updates. GitHub Actions CI runs security scans.

name: CC6.8.3 Security Awareness and Malware Response Procedures
description:
The organization shall provide security awareness training to all personnel covering recognition of phishing attempts, social engineering tactics, and safe handling of files from external sources. A documented incident response procedure shall exist for malware detection events, including immediate containment steps, notification requirements, and remediation actions. Given the small team size, cross-training shall ensure multiple team members can execute response procedures.

Implementation: Training covers phishing, malware. IR procedure includes containment steps.
